title: Waist-to-height splines do not reliably improve cross-cohort FVC prediction beyond flexible waist and height
abstract: We evaluated whether height-normalized waist supplies transferable predictive structure beyond conventional anthropometry. A source-fitted spline ridge predictor of concurrent forced vital capacity (FVC) used age, height, BMI, waist, sex, race/ethnicity and smoking. Adding waist-to-height spline terms and their sex interactions was tested in separately recruited NHANES cohorts:2007–2008 training (n=3662) and2011–2012 frozen evaluation (n=3603). Examination-weighted target MSE was 0.26740501 versus 0.26754998 L², difference +0.00014497 L², joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.00118708,+0.00342865]. Ratio augmentation improved a weaker BMI-based comparator descriptively, but failed the registered improvement criterion beyond flexible waist. This exploratory inconclusive negative result does not establish equivalence or disprove abdominal-adiposity information. Different recruitment cohorts within one survey program do not establish independent-program validation.
